newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end down on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end down on weak sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down on Thursday on weak market sentiment, traders said.
The key November 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 3,260 yuan ($393) per tonne, losing 16 yuan. It opened at 3,270 and hit a high of 3,280.
July fell 13 to 3,299 yuan per tonne, September 38 to 3,250, the January 1998 contract rose 25 to 3,240 and March shed 16 to 3,280.
Combined volume fell to 21,300 tonnes from 23,700.
Soybeans opened mostly lower and moved around opening levels for most of the session, traders said.
"Most investors are pessimistic about the future market trend given the weak performance over the past few trading days," one trader said.
"Over-supply of spot soybeans has also made investors reluctant to hold long positions," he said.
Traders said they expected soybeans to fall further on Friday.
